summary: Ross Arthur Leslie Moore was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Dulwich College (~1874–1880) and Peterhouse, Cambridge (~1880–1884), where he later served as Lecturer in Marathi from 1921 to 1927.

Ross Bolleter works in Buddhist studies. He earned a bachelor's degree at the University of Western Australia under David Tunley (~1964–1967) and trained under John Tarrant and Robert Baker Aitken (1982–1992), later teaching at the Zen Group of Western Australia (~1985–2023).

Rotem Geva is a historian and Indologist. She earned an M.A. from The New School (2005–2007) and a Ph.D. from Princeton University (2007–2014), and served as Department Chair at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem in 2016.

Roy Rappaport worked in religious studies and related fields. He earned his doctorate at Columbia University (~1959–1966), chaired the Department of Anthropology at the University of Michigan (~1965–1997), and served as past president of the American Anthropological Association (~1987–1989).

Roy Tzohar works in philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tel Aviv University (~1997–2004) and earned his PhD at Columbia University (~2004–2011) under Gary A. Tubb. He has held appointments at Tel Aviv University, becoming Associate Professor in 2024.

Roy W. Perrett is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at the University of Canterbury (~1973–1977) and the University of Otago (~1978–1982). He held posts at Massey University (~1987–2001), University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (~2001–2010), and University of Melbourne (~2011).

Royal W. Weiler was an Indologist and linguist who earned his B.A. and Ph.D. under W. Norman Brown at the University of Pennsylvania (~1948–1956). He taught at Columbia University (~1957–1963) and the University of Pennsylvania (~1963–1978).

Royall Tyler is a scholar of Japanology and religious studies who earned degrees from Harvard and Columbia, completing a doctorate under Donald Keene. He taught at Ohio State, Wisconsin-Madison, Oslo, Harvard, and headed the Japan Centre at Australian National University (1990–2000).
Royce Wiles is an Indologist who completed his PhD at the Australian National University by 2000 and subsequently held a post there.

Rozaliya Osipovna Shor was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Vsevolod Miller. She was a researcher at RANION, GAKhN, and the Institute of Oriental Studies, and served as professor at Baku State, IKP, MIFLI, MSPU, and LIFLI.

Ruben L. F. Habito works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Ateneo de Manila, the University of Tokyo, and Sophia University, training under Koun Yamada. He held posts at Sophia, Ryukoku, and Southern Methodist University (1989), and founded Maria Kannon Zen Center.

Rudi Paret was a scholar of religious studies and related fields. He studied at the University of Tübingen (~1920–1924) and held academic posts at the University of Bonn (~1930–1941) and the University of Tübingen (~1941–1968).

Rudolf Carnap was a philosopher who studied at Jena, Freiburg, Berlin, and Vienna. He held academic posts at the University of Vienna (1926), Charles University (1931), the University of Chicago (1936–1952), and the University of California, Los Angeles (1954).

Rudolf Ernst Wilhelm Meyer was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Heidelberg University (1873) and earned his Ph.D. at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1874–1877) under Johannes Schmidt and doctoral supervisor Albrecht Weber.

Rudolf Fuchs was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. at Humboldt University of Berlin by 1908 under doctoral supervisor Richard Pischel, alongside instruction from teachers including Albrecht Weber, Emil Sieg, and Heinrich Zimmer.
Rudolf Geiger studied at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1913–1917) and held an academic post at the University of Munich (~1937–1958).

Rudolf Haym was a scholar of philosophy and history who studied at Cöllnisches Gymnasium, Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1839), and Frederick William University Berlin (~1841–1843). He held a post at Halle-Wittenberg in 1868.

Rudolf Kaschewsky was a scholar of Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Universities of Bonn and Cologne, taught Tibetan at Goethe University Frankfurt, and served at the University of Bonn (1974–2004).
Rudolf Lange was a scholar in Japanology and linguistics. He held academic posts at the University of Tokyo (~1874–1881) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1887–1920).

Rudolf Meringer was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Vienna and Humboldt University of Berlin under Johannes Schmidt. He held posts at the University of Vienna (1885, 1892) and the University of Graz (1899–1930).
